ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The central atom in the figure is a carbon, connected upward to an O marked with a negative sign, leftward to R1, down-left to R2, and rightward to SiR3; there is a curved arrow beside it, but the problem requires ignoring the arrow. Reasoning: After ignoring the arrow, the connectivity can be written as an O-C-Si main chain, and the central carbon also has two unspecified substituents R1 and R2, while silicon also has one unspecified substituent R3. Use the SMILES wildcard * to represent these unspecified substituents; starting from the wildcard on silicon gives *[Si]C, adding two wildcard branches (*)(*) on the carbon and then attaching O gives *[Si]C(*)(*)O.

method.method_draft: First describe the visual structure as a connectivity graph: O-C-Si is the main chain, with two additional unspecified substituents on the carbon and an unspecified substituent associated with the silicon group. Ignore the curved arrow because the question instructs to do so. Encode the Si-C-O connectivity in SMILES starting from a wildcard substituent on silicon as '*[Si]C', then add the two carbon R groups as branches '(*)(*)', and finish with the O attached to carbon, giving '*[Si]C(*)(*)O'.
